cards.explanation: The answer is False. Peter's reason is the time of day: “It is only the third hour of the day!” Nothing in his words says it's late at night. The third hour is Peter's whole case, friends.

The answer is all people. Peter quotes Joel, a prophet, and God says, “…I will pour out My Spirit on all people.” Then the list keeps going: sons, daughters, young men, old men, and even servants. God's list has no VIP section.

The answer is True. Joel's words, as Peter quotes them, end with this: “And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.” Wonders in the sky come first, but the promise is what lands last. Everyone who calls, saved.

The answer is God's. Peter says Jesus “…was delivered up by God’s set plan and foreknowledge…” Then he says the crowd, by the hands of the lawless, put Him to death. He holds both truths in the same breath, and he doesn't blink.

The answer is True. Peter says, “But God raised Him from the dead, releasing Him from the agony of death, because it was impossible for death to keep Him in its grip.” Impossible, friends. Death had its grip out and couldn't hold on.

The answer is glad. David says, “Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will dwell in hope…” That's from Psalm 16, and Peter quotes it. David's heart is glad, his tongue is joining in, and the rest of him is hopeful.

The answer is the Christ rising from the dead. Peter says David was a prophet and, “Foreseeing this, David spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that He was not abandoned to Hades, nor did His body see decay.” David's tomb was still right there, so his words pointed to Someone else. Peter says God has raised this Jesus.
The answer is False. Peter says, “God has raised this Jesus to life, to which we are all witnesses.” It's “we,” not just “I.” Peter stood up with the Eleven, and he says “all.”

The answer is Jesus. Peter says, “Exalted, then, to the right hand of God, He has received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what you now see and hear.” The “He” is Jesus. Peter has just said God raised this Jesus, so the pieces line up.

The answer is Lord. Peter says, “Therefore let all Israel know with certainty that God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ!” That's the whole sermon landing in one sentence. And he says it with certainty.

The answer is “Brothers, what shall we do?” The people were cut to the heart, and they asked Peter and the other apostles that very question. It's a question about what to do next. Peter replies in the very next verse.

The answer is repent and be baptized. Peter says, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins…” Hear that “…every one of you…” Nobody gets a pass, and nobody gets left out.

The answer is sins. Peter says to be baptized “…in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins…” He also says they'll receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. Forgiveness and a gift in the same sentence is a lot of good news.

The answer is False. Peter says, “This promise belongs to you and your children and to all who are far off…” and then adds, “…to all whom the Lord our God will call to Himself.” The promise isn't only for the crowd. It goes out to their children and to those who are far off.
The answer is False. The text says, “…about three thousand were added to the believers that day.” That is a LOT of people added in a single day, friends. I'd lose count somewhere around forty.

The answer is awe. The text says, “A sense of awe came over everyone, and the apostles performed many wonders and signs.” Awe is that hush when you realize something bigger than you is happening. Everyone felt it, and nobody was left out.

The answer is True. The text says, “Selling their possessions and goods, they shared with anyone who was in need.” They'd just heard the good news, and they shared with whoever needed it. I'd have been checking my own shelves for spare chocolate chips.

The answer is that the Lord adds to their number those being saved. The text says, “And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” Daily, not just on Pentecost. The believers are praising God, and He keeps adding people.
